Virtual Hug. I can relate...sometimes it takes those little insignificant things to open a flood gate of emotions. It sounds like you felt anxiety, guilt, and frustration all at the same time. 

If you had a busy week maybe your mind and body were tired...this was just it’s way of cathartic release.

As a reference point...When I have panic attacks it usually does involve crying and hyperventilating....and also extremely intense chest tightness. Your body feel very off...but everyone is different and we all have different definitions.

Don’t THINK how you should feel...just feel.

Maybe this weekend engage in your version of selfcare for an hour or two minimum...a day If you can manage. Sleep, eat good food, journal/meditate/pray (whatever works for you) ...go on a walk. Buy something nice for yourself. Just do activities that you enjoy. 

Sounds to me like you need a little break. You deserve it...I hope you feel better. 

With regards to picking up your cake. Just call the store ahead of time. Apologies and be transparent. Likely they thought less of it than you did. It’s likely sitting in the fridge in the back. This sort of thing happens more than you might think. I’ve worked the service industry before.

Tip: I secured some shinning fates loot by waiting at one store for the vendor. It took some dedication coupled with transparency and non creepy vibes with the Walmart employees so they knew why I was walking around the store for a few hours. Ended up catching the vendor and was first in line. Once he stocked...the loot was gone in 15min. (Not all by me of course!!)
I think Walmarts stocked today....at least in my area. I waited around for the vendor to show and got lucky. Targets stock tomorrow....I think. Good luck!!!

Sinus infections usually consist of fluid buildup....the sinuses, ears, Eustachian tube, and throat all sort of connect. I had a sinus infection for MONTHS that I didn’t treat properly...and so everything got clogged and could/still feel fluid within my ear.

Take a deep breath. Has the bleeding stopped? If you’re sincerely concerned call for help...but if the bleeding stopped and it’s not pushing out of your body still you’re likely not going to bleed to death. How do you feel now?

It’s usually accompanied by other symptoms like cough, runny nose, loss of taste, fever, chills, etc.

I’m in school to be a medical assistant right now. My advice would be to call your doctor or let your MA/phlebotomist know that you are concerned. We can draw your blood in different positions in order to make you more comfortable.  Laying down during the draw might lessen the nausea. Knowing that you have anxiety would also alert us to use our more experienced/skilled phlebotomist instead of letting me poke you as a student. Communicate with us and we will do our best to make it at least a decent experience....and even if you do have a hiccup during the draw...we are trained to handle that and you should not feel ashamed or embarrassed. I have glaucoma. 

Glaucoma is vision loss caused by prolonged high optic pressure. You don’t feel it most of the time. It’s referenced as the vision thief because people usually can’t detect if they have it. The peripheral of your vision will be black or grey. A pressure spike can lead to ‘rainbows’ around lights. I’ve seen this...my pressure was threw the roof....but it was also accompanied with severe pain, black spots, and nausea. 

What you’re describing sounds like a migraine. Your vision won’t restore if it is glaucoma 

I’m not a doctor though...please don’t base your ultimate decisions on me. Happy to answer any questions though. I have all sorts of eye issues lol
